A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same BA-LoRA research by the same authors. Text, equations, tables and figures are readable throughout. V1 ends with references and has no appendix; v2 includes readable Appendices A–D, supporting a complete comparison.

before.justification: V1 reports original BA-LoRA evaluations on generation, understanding and out-of-domain tasks in Tables 2–5 and Figure 1. Some comparator results are explicitly borrowed from PiSSA, but the reported outcomes are not solely attributed to other work.

after.justification: V2 retains the original benchmark results and reports additional regularizer ablations, rank experiments, model comparisons and feature visualizations in the main text and Appendix C.

M1.justification: The PiSSA initialization and three-regularizer framework remain. However, Equation 12 removes the NLG singular-value variance term, leaving only the normalized top-k singular-value sum. Equations 10–11 also make token conditioning and temporal averaging explicit, without establishing whether those clarifications reflect a changed implementation.

E1.justification: The mathematics, coding, instruction-following, GLUE and GLUE-X training and evaluation coverage is retained. Appendix B supplies constituent-dataset descriptions, while the new visualizations use existing MNLI coverage. Its WNLI listing does not establish an additional evaluated task; larger models and quantization change configurations rather than dataset or task coverage.

E2.justification: The comparator sets in the retained benchmark tables are unchanged. V2 Figure 3 adds evaluated QLoRA and QPiSSA comparisons against QBA-LoRA for Mixtral-8x7B and LLaMA-3-70B configurations; these quantized comparators were absent from v1 Figure 1.

E3.justification: The model comparison expands from six backbones to ten, adding larger dense models, mixture-of-experts models and quantized configurations. Appendix C.2 introduces ranks 1–128 under one-epoch MetaMathQA-100K training, and the new ablations and MNLI visualizations introduce component controls and feature-sampling procedures. The retained main benchmark budgets and metrics remain substantially unchanged.

E4.justification: V2 adds single-regularizer versus unregularized and full-method ablations on GSM8K/MATH (Figure 2), rank sensitivity experiments (Figure 4), and MNLI feature-separation analyses with training trajectories (Figures 1 and 5–8). These investigate component contributions, rank dependence and representation dynamics that v1 did not analyze. The existing GLUE-X evaluation is retained.

E5.justification: V1 gives no repeated-run or seed counts. V2 Section 4.3 newly describes results as averages of three independent experiments, and Appendix B.4 specifies three random seeds per GLUE task for BERT-L and GPT-2-XL. This establishes changed reporting, not an increase in runs; confidence intervals, dispersion estimates and significance tests remain absent.

E6.justification: V1 Tables 2–5 retain their numerical values as v2 Tables 1–4, but v2 adds substantial ablation, rank, larger-model, quantized-model and visualization results. The expanded model plot also changes existing GSM8K bars: Gemma's BA-LoRA result moves from approximately 78% to 80%, while v2 Table 1 still reports 78.13%. This is an unexplained reporting difference, not an established comparable-setting performance gain.

T1.justification: Equation 12 substantively revises the mathematical definition of the NLG spectral regularizer by removing its variance component. Equations 10–11 introduce explicit conditional, length-normalized expressions. The PiSSA decomposition and NLU regularizer mathematics otherwise remain, and neither version provides theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: The central claims of mitigating catastrophic inheritance and outperforming LoRA/PiSSA through three regularizers remain. V2's conclusion adds the explicit claim that the regularizers are effective individually as well as jointly. The change from Bias-Aware to Bias-Alleviating does not itself change the scientific contribution.

C2.justification: V2 interprets feature separation as evidence of mitigating inherited imbalance and adds explanations of individual regularizer contributions and rank dependence. Its NLG spectral explanation shifts from smoothing singular values to emphasizing principal components. Appendix D additionally identifies untested fairness and societal-stereotype effects and regularizer-specific computational overhead, extending v1's language, resource and tuning limitations.

D1.justification: Appendix B adds BERT/GPT-2 training settings, GLUE-X transfer procedures and evaluation-framework references. However, v1's complete GLUE hyperparameter table is replaced by less specific prose, and its k = 0.3 setting disappears. Appendix B.3 states rank 8 despite the retained main-text NLU rank 128. Section 7 also promises code and weights upon acceptance while the abstract still says code is available.

R1.justification: New Appendix A substantially expands the context around dataset bias, label noise, fairness and prior PEFT approaches, including works by Northcutt, Mehrabi and the authors of BitFit and AdapterFusion. Section 3.2.3 adds explicit connections to Dong et al. on robust fine-tuning and Gat et al. on entropy regularization. The original PEFT-family positioning is largely retained.

P1.justification: V2 rewrites substantial portions of the abstract, introduction, related work, NLG explanation and conclusion, and renames the method and title. It merges dataset/model introductions, moves the model-size analysis and limitations into an organized appendix, and adds ethics and reproducibility sections. These materially change the narrative and document organization.

P2.justification: V2 adds extensive t-SNE panels, ablation bar charts and rank curves, and redraws and relocates v1 Figure 1 as the expanded Figure 3. It removes the GLUE hyperparameter table, adds model/dataset summary tables, and reformats retained result tables with shaded BA-LoRA rows. The document template and heading presentation also change.

improvement.justification: The new ablations and rank studies address v1's missing evidence about component contributions and sensitivity. However, v2 loses explicit hyperparameters, introduces conflicting settings and leaves changed GSM8K bars unreconciled with retained tables. Its ablation interpretation also overstates the evidence: Figure 2 reports Mistral SVD-only MATH accuracy of 21.58 versus 21.72 without regularization, contradicting the claim that the unregularized model always performs worst. These substantive gains and new reproducibility and consistency problems prevent a reliable net-quality judgment.
